accuracy.evidence: Checked against Common Core 3.MD.C.7d ('Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas') and its progression document (Common Core Standards Writing Team, Progressions for Geometric Measurement, 2012), and the DfE National Curriculum in England mathematics programmes of study for Years 4 to 6 (area by counting squares, area of rectangles in cm² and m², then compound shapes). Every number was recomputed: the 8 by 6 grid L with a 3 by 4 corner missing covers 48 − 12 = 36 squares; cutting down at x = 5 gives 5 × 6 + 3 × 2 = 30 + 6 and across at y = 4 gives 5 × 4 + 8 × 2 = 20 + 16, both 36; the 10 cm by 7 cm L with a 6 by 3 corner missing has steps 10 − 4 = 6 and 7 − 4 = 3 and area 70 − 18 = 52 = 4 × 7 + 6 × 4; every parameterised answer was checked at the corners of its ranges by gate_items.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors in the area literature (Outhred and Mitchelmore on area measurement; the Common Core progression's notes on decomposition; NCETM Year 5 and 6 area guidance): multiplying the two longest sides as if the corner were present (step 1 predict, p1, tag box), confusing area with perimeter by adding sides (step 1 predict, m4, tags addsides and unit), adding a missing side instead of subtracting (missing-side buttons 14 and 11, p3, tag addmiss), cuts that do not make rectangles (four position-specific cut messages, m1, tags anycut and diag), double counting an overlap (m6, tags overlap and small), adding the corner in the subtract method (step 5 predict, tag addcut), and thinking different cuts give different areas (step 3 predict, m2, tags two and biggest).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 964 Perimeter of Compound Shapes walks round the edge; 716 Area and the Distributive Property cuts a plain rectangle; 507 and 661 tile rectangles. This lab is about rectilinear shapes with a missing corner: painting an L cell by cell, a draggable cut line that is judged by whether each piece is a rectangle, the same total from two cut directions, unmarked inside steps found from the opposite sides, and a fill-then-remove subtract method.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each rule by doing: the painted count stops at 36, not 48; a cut in the wrong place keeps the L visible and the message says which piece still has a step; when the cut is right the pieces colour in with their own length × width; making both cuts puts 30 + 6 = 36 and 20 + 16 = 36 side by side; choosing 14 for a step is caught because 14 is longer than the whole shape; filling the big rectangle first makes the 70 − 18 order concrete.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 asks the L's area with '8 × 6 = 48 cm²' tempting; painting stops at 36. Step 3 asks whether the other cut changes the total with 'different, because the pieces change' tempting; both cuts give 36. Step 5 asks for the L's area from 70 and 18 with '70 + 18 = 88 cm²' tempting; removing the corner gives 52.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Every distractor in the eight challenge questions has its own tag and message in carea_art.js WHY: box, addsides, times, bigger, two, biggest, addmiss, copy, addcut, nocut, unit, cube, anycut, diag, overlap and small. In the lab each slip is named: four separate wrong-cut messages by direction and side, specific messages for choosing 14 or 4 and 11 or 4 for the missing steps, a message for painting a square in the missing corner, and a message for removing the corner before filling the big rectangle.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 2.6 (limit 6.5) and the adult text 6.4 (limit 9.5). Kid sentences are short and concrete ('Find each area with length times width. Then add the two areas.'); the precise terms for the band (area, square centimetre, cm², rectilinear, compound shape, decompose, opposite sides) are in the key idea and adult text.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. The four kid paragraphs match the counting, cutting, missing-side and take-away steps; the adult text gives the standard, what each task shows with its numbers, and the named mistakes; every hint points to a count, cut, side or step in the lab.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android, 2x) for every step at start, mid Show me and end, in light and dark themes, plus desktop. After the first pass the two ? tags were moved onto the shape beside their own edges and each missing edge is drawn as a dashed purple line until found, and the follow-up message was reworded. Grid squares are about 37 px on a phone, the cut snaps to grid lines, and every action also has a full-width button.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, all 5 tasks complete with Show me, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Paint the next row, Move the cut left/right or up/down, Turn the cut, Cut here, inside step across/down with each length, Fill the big rectangle, Take away the corner), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the number of squares painted, the cut position and direction, the pieces' areas, the side found, and the big rectangle and corner areas.
